utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I first have to apologise for the late start. It's exclusively due to me misjudging the time this morning. When working, I thought it was 8.00, and then it turned out to be 9.00 already. Apologies for that, especially because I'm the one who is now and then criticising the parties for not being precise. I have to improve my own performance in that respect as well. Apart from that, Mr. Farr, are you ready? By the way, there is one matter, and I think the attention has already been drawn to it by Chambers staff and it has been communicated with Mr. Jordash, that there is D293 MFI'd, which might, in terms of authenticity, might be resolved with this witness. Mr. Farr, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps I should first do my daily routine. Mr. Micic, you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, you told us yesterday that Radenko Novakovic was one of the employees of the State Security Service who was in Bosnia in late 1995, and that's at transcript page 49 from yesterday. Can you tell us why Radenko Novakovic was in Bosnia in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main reason for his stay there was the establishment of a stationary intelligence post in the territory of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately what month he was there, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly how long he was there. I can just say that I probably saw him at the very beginning of the year. I mean the very beginning of 1995, or the end of 1994, because it was cold. I remember what the weather was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You saw him in Bosnia at that time, or you saw him in Belgrade at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnia. Bosnia, yes. Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit P2543 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, while this is coming up, I'll just tell you that this is an excerpt from a notebook kept by Ratko Mladic, and this particular entry is dated 22 September 1995. Now, if we take a look at this first page, we can see that this entry records a meeting with the organs of the Main Staff of the VRS and the commanders of various units. The meeting occurred in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And if we could please have page 4 in both languages, in the middle of the page. Here on page 4 we can see that General Milovanovic is beginning his briefing. And if we can turn to page 5. If we can turn to the next page of the document in both languages, we'll see that General Milovanovic's briefing continues.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And I'll read now a portion beginning with the words "A team from the Serbian DB." "A team from the Serbian DB appeared here. Filipovic, Bozovic, as well as Kijac and Kovac, and Krajisnik told us that 3 brigades would come. Bozovic said that the VJ would not and that the RS MUP decided that 1.200 fighters would come, be incorporated into the 1st Krajina Corps, and used like all other units." The fact that Filipovic and Bozovic came to Bosnia was corroborated by General Milovanovic himself during his testimony in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that's transcript page 15522 to 15527.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, you told us yesterday that you were not aware of members of the DB of Serbia meeting with senior officers of the VRS in the second half of 1995. Are you able to say why you are not aware of this?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was not aware of that because I hadn't been informed about it. I mean, I personally did not have any information available with regard to those matters. Now, what the real reason was for this information not being accessible to me is something I cannot assess either.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that meeting with General Milovanovic was outside of Mr. Filipovic's regular duties as the deputy head of the 2nd Administration of the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't dare claim something like that unequivocally. I really do not know in which capacity Dragan Filipovic as deputy head of the 2nd Administration took part in any kind of discussions of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we now please have Exhibit P2546 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, this is another entry from one of Ratko Mladic's notebooks. This entry is dated 3 October 1995, and it's entitled "Meeting with Dragan Filipovic aka Fica, Radojica Bozovic." The entry indicates that Filipovic spoke first, and it records him as saying: "Arkan's men are operating under the control of Pecanac, and in my opinion they're doing a good job." Now, you told us yesterday that Dragan Filipovic was your immediate superior at this time. Do you know why it would be your immediate superior, the deputy chief of the 2nd Administration of the DB of Serbia, who would be informing Ratko Mladic about the deployment of Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I cannot even intimate what the reasons were for this kind of activity, and in particular, I do not know who it was that he submitted reports to in that respect, namely that Arkan's men were operating properly. And I don't know what this means, operating properly. I mean, in what sense? Also, the name Pecanac doesn't tell me a thing, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, I heard in translation the word "properly" used various times. I do not find that in the text. Could you please seek to verify what exactly the witness is referring to, because it seems that the written translation is either different or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, as His Honour Judge Orie just indicated, you used the word -- well, what you said, that Arkan's men were operating properly. Can you tell us which portion of the text you were referring to when you referred to Arkan's men operating properly?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's practically the first sentence after the first bullet point. It says "Arkan's men," and there's a reference to Pecanac, and then it is stated that he thinks that they are operating properly. Now, I don't know what sense that he meant that, that they were operating properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The word "properly" is, of course, not exactly the same as it is translated in writing, doing a good job, and behaving properly is, I would say, not identical, and I suggest to the parties that we have this translation verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: We'll do that, Your Honour. Could we now please have 65 ter 6175 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document on the heading of the security department of the Eastern Bosnia Corps Command, and it's dated the 20th of September, 1995. Are you able to recognise the format of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not. The format is dispatch format, that's for sure. The State Security Department used a slightly different format at that time, but I assume it is a dispatch. The State Security Department had a marking, DX. That meant that it was extremely urgent, and that seems to be missing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: During your time in the DB did you have a chance to see military intelligence reports?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military intelligence?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Closer co-operation happened only later, towards the end of 1998 and up until mid-1999. Before that, I did not have an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd like to read the first few lines of this report starting at the beginning of the first paragraph. It says: "In the evening hours of 19 September 1995, at a working meeting of the Bijeljina SO, or Municipal Assembly, which was attended among others by Mr. Frenki and Bozovic from the MUP of the Republic of Serbia and Zeljko Raznjatovic, aka Arkan, on one side and Mr. Kozic, the prime minister of RS, Minister Boro Bosic, and organs of the authorities of the Bijeljina region on the other, it was allegedly agreed that Arkan and his unit should take and liberate Teocak." Sir, are you able to tell us anything about the presence of Mr. Simatovic and Mr. Bozovic at this meeting on 19 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge whatsoever about the information presented except for the following: As far as I know, Bozovic was never an employee of the Ministry of the Interior, if we mean the same Bozovic, if we have the same Bozovic in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to stop you there. I apologise for interrupting, but I think that you've already answered the substance of my question which is that you received the award for --

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: whether you'd received an award from the JSO, and my question was from the JSO, you said no, and then -- at transcript page 47. And then slightly later, at page 62, you indicated that you may have received a lighter at some point from the service. Is there a reason you didn't mention the award of this pistol at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The pistol was presented to me, and to this day this is my belief, and I have a decision on this award, that it was given to me by the chief of the State Security Department. That is why I don't even have to pay taxes for that pistol. So it's not the JSO. It's the chief of the State Security Department at the proposal made by my supervisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know why Franko Simatovic and Dragan Filipovic were receiving awards on this day?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, really I cannot say. I mean, I don't know anything specific. I can talk about the persons who were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Were you aware that they had received these awards on this day?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Believe me, no. Because these are completely different places. I mean where awards are handed out. I know about these young men and these young women who are mentioned here underneath this list. I mean, I know the reasons why the awards were given for that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Which -- which people are you referring to there? Who were you referring -- for which people? Do you know the reason why they received the awards?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One, two, and three, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Of which -- of which list? Of the third list, the monetary reward list?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the awards handed out in the centre of the security -- State Security Department of Belgrade, I know of the monetary award given to the first person, then the person mentioned under number 5, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And why did they receive awards?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basis was the same: for special efforts made in breaking the network of agents of Croatia and the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, could I ask one question. Why didn't you mention the pistol you received, yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was whether I received a pistol from the JSO, or at least I wasn't aware of that, because the decision that was issued in my name specified that it would be -- that it was being presented by the head of the State Security Department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I do agree with you that the first question was about receiving an award from the JSO. However, in your answers and in the follow-up questions, the question was not limited in any way to the JSO any more, because when you told us that you had received a lighter, a lighter of bad quality, you did not tell us that you received it from the JSO. You told us that it was a lighter with the -- I think the emblem of the service, and you told us that others got similar lighters not from the JSO but from the service itself, but by far more -- it seems to me that it's far more important when you officially get a pistol. Why didn't you tell us, and why were you emphasising so much that the lighters were of bad quality and it was totally unsignificant when you are not talking about the JSO? You are talking about an award or at least something you received from the service as a sign of appreciation of your work, and you were silent on the pistol. Do you have an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question to which I gave the answer you just quoted was whether I was aware the kinds of awards conferred by the JSO, and in response to that question I mentioned that I knew of awards such as knives and daggers, symbolic daggers, of course, not real ones, that I never received myself. And a pistol, I still assert, is an award received from the State Security Department independently of the JSO. And I stated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the record, and we can read exactly what you said about -- in answer to questions specifically on receiving anything from the JSO and how you elaborated on matters, objects, you did not receive from the JSO, explaining very much how insignificant it was what you received from the service, from the RDB, and then I said: "Let's be practical. The lighters, the lighters with the emblem of the department, would you buy them at the department shop, or were they given as a kind of an appreciation of work done?" That has got nothing to do with the JSO anymore, and at least your answer was: "I had a lighter like that. Quite simply, they were received." We were not talking about the JSO any more. We were talking about the service. "I had a lighter like that, too, but it didn't work for very long." You were emphasising the insignificance, and your answer was not the whole truth to the extent that you had not told us that apart from a bad functioning lighter you received officially a pistol. Any comment on what I just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose it must be my bad interpretation. Yes, I received all the awards from the department. I can enumerate them all now regardless of the lighter and the rest. Quite simply, I stated that because I wasn't clear about the origin of those lighters, whether they belonged to the JSO or the department. At one point even the emblems were quite the same. That's the main reason. But I did receive other awards for my work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You now even tell us that you may have received the lighter from the JSO, which you didn't tell us yesterday. But, Mr. Farr, you may proceed. Please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, looking at the bottom of the page, we see three individuals were being given an award posthumously, Radoslav Kostic, Milan Dimic, and Zeljko Torbica. And I would now like to take a quick look at some information relating to one of those individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And for that can we please have 65 ter 6289 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a personnel file of Zeljko Torbica, one of the individuals we just saw receiving a posthumous award on the security day in 1996, and I'd just like to read a brief portion of the information we see here on the first page. It says: "Zeljko Torbica, son of Radomir and Kadivka, nee Milivojevic, a Serb, single, a photographic technician. He joined the police in Knin as a volunteer on 27 July 1991. On 1 August 1991, he began his training in a special unit of the Krajina MUP and took part in several battles with this unit. On 24 September 1991, he was admitted into the Special-Purpose Unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, where he carried out the duties of an instructor and squad commander. He was killed on 22nd June, 1992, during fighting near Brcko and was buried on 24 June 1992 at the cemetery in Smederevska Palanka." Now, my question is: Do you know why a person with this particular history would be receiving an award from the Serbian DB on the same day as you in 1996?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't because I don't know this person or the reasons why he was given an award.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's likely that the Prosecution will be tendering this personnel file from the bar table in rebuttal, so we would ask for it to be marked for identification under seal at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Objection to the Prosecution's application. The fact that the Prosecution intend to apply to tender it pursuant to rebuttal evidence isn't basis for MFI'ing a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the need to -- I mean, you've read part of the document. Is there any dispute as to whether Mr. Farr read from the personnel file of this person? Apart from -- there's no dispute about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Farr read out everything correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honour, it's not necessary. We'll just bring our bar table motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The evidence we received apart from that is that the witness doesn't know this person, but there's no dispute as apparently this being the content of that document read out by Mr. Farr. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we please move back to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can we now please have Exhibit P352 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a certificate dated the 4th of January, 1994, and if we can start by zooming in on the initials in the top right corner on the B/C/S version. Sir, here once again we see the initials of Franko Simatovic that you identified for us yesterday; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. If we could zoom back out, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, this document is signed by Milan Radonjic as the deputy commander of the JATD, and I'll just read the beginning of the document. It says: "Subject: Certificate confirming that Vasilije Mijovic is a member of the ATD unit of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia." And now, sir, I want to read something from your testimony yesterday, and this comes from pages 50 to 51. It starts with my question. "Q. Did you ever learn anything about a possible professional relationship between a person named Mijovic and Mr. Simatovic? "A. As for the direct relations, whatever we call them, I really cannot qualify them in any way because I didn't have any information as to whether they were professional or something else, especially because I first heard of Mr. Mijovic in the context of that well-known, I know it is well-known here, celebration in Kula in 1997. "Q. So you had never heard of Mijovic any time before the celebration in Kula in 1997; is that your evidence? "A. Yes, precisely." Sir, do you maintain that you never heard of Vaso Mijovic until 1997 in light of this document confirming his membership in the JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still maintain that I had no information whatsoever about that person, and the first I learned anything about Mr. Mijovic was at the celebration in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Before we continue, I just received one of -- the result of the verification of one of the lines I asked for, and I only read the line which now gives the translation without errors, and I read it to you. The answer to a question yesterday in the accurate translation is: "I can only repeat what I stated earlier. I would need a lot of time and material to even recall who Tomislav Kovac was. I have no closer or better knowledge. At the time when we first mentioned him, I didn't even know who he was." Whereas earlier the translation was "when I first met him," but apparently it's a reference to when Mr. Kovac was first mentioned. I thought it good to already inform you about the outcome of the verification. And also I would like to stress how important it sometimes is to seek verification if there is any disputes about what was said or how it was translated. Please proceed, Mr. Farr. And, Mr. Micic, you've heard that we verified part of an answer you gave yesterday which caused some question marks, but there was a mistake, and we always do that if there's a real problem in translations or what someone has said. Then listening to audio and verifying the accuracy of translation and transcription finally will give us the answer, and in this case a mistake was made and it has now been corrected. Mr. Farr, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would now like to turn back briefly to Mr. Simatovic's mission to the Krajina in 1991, and if we could please have P2615 on the screen. And if we can have the second page in English and zoom in on the bottom of the first page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, just to orient you, this is a statement dated the 7th of May, 1992, by a man named Milenko Sucevic, who at that time was the commander of the communications company of the Main Staff of the Territorial Defence of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And if we could now return to the top of the document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'll start reading at the beginning of this document and we'll see that this statement actually relates to events in 1991. So starting at the beginning, the statement says: "In April last year, I was holding the post of Chief of Communications in the special units of the Krajina SUP stationed in the Golubic Youth Colony. Late in April, we received four Land Rover vehicles for communication purposes equipped with the Racal radio devices from the Serbian MUP in Belgrade. The equipment of each vehicle also included a trailer with a generator. There were no teletype machines in the vehicles. I took over the vehicles from Dragan Jerenic who was in charge of communications in the Serbian MUP." Sir, there's been other evidence in this case that at least as of February 1992 Dragan Jerenic was, in fact, a member of the Serbian DB, specifically the 4th Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that's P2626.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with this person Dragan Jerenic?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The first two sentences of what I just read indicate that in April of 1991, the special units of the Krajina SUP at Golubic received communications equipment from the Serbian MUP. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, although I'm familiar with the Racal radio device, although I don't know how to use it, but I know it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the Racal radio device is a device for two-way communication rather than surveillance?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, it was used solely to maintain communication between two points, but I repeat again, I never used it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Skipping down a couple of lines, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll just ask you and the other parties whether this last answer can be understood as affirmative. Surveillance is catching something from the air or receiving it, whereas two-way communication is sending, receiving, and then sending back. That's how I understand it. And what the witness says is a -- the way in which it was used, which I understand is affirmative of what Mr. Farr has asked the witness. If the parties agree, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I can see no reason to disagree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I see Mr. Bakrac also nod. Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Skipping down a couple of lines, I'll start reading with the words "After approximately two months." "After approximately two months, there was a need for Land Rover vehicles, and pursuant to an order by Frenk (the chief representative of the Serbian MUP), I dismantled the entire equipment from two of the vehicles and moved them to two Lada Niva vehicles which we had taken over from the Elektrodistribucija Knin and ZTP Knin companies pursuant to an order signed by Milan Martic. The emptied Land Rovers were used to tow mortars and transport the crews in the area of Velika Glava." Sir, our position is that this document shows that Franko Simatovic was doing more in the Krajina than just conducting surveillance against Captain Dragan. In fact, he was co-operating with the special units of the SAO Krajina Police and was co-operating with them closely enough that the chief of communications of the special units of the Krajina SUP was willing to follow Mr. Simatovic's instructions regarding equipment provided by the Serbian MUP. Are you able to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning your position as stated, I could really say nothing. I couldn't put forward any information or facts. But as far as this document is concerned, it just says that this gentleman, what's his name, acted on the instructions of Frenk --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Do you know anything about it? Then please tell us. If you do not know about it, then leave it to us to interpret the document unless you have any specific information which would assist us, not start interpreting the document yourself without such additional information. Please proceed, Mr. Farr. May I then take it that you do not have any -- Witness, you do not have any additional information which would assist us in better understanding the document? It's just that you started interpret it on its face value. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I move on to my next document, just to avoid confusion, I'd like to clarify something I just said. I said our position is that the document shows that Frenki Simatovic was doing more in the Krajina than just conducting surveillance against Captain Dragan. It's our position that he was not in fact conducting surveillance against Captain Dragan in the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So, sir, perhaps if you'd care to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You understand what the question is, Mr. Micic? That is, that not only that he did more, but he only did things other than surveilling Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really could not confirm that on the basis of anything I know. And I read this document a bit differently, but that doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again there seems to be some misunderstanding. If my recollection serves me well, you said yesterday that Mr. Simatovic was there because there was an important matter of the surveillance of Mr. -- of Captain Dragan, if I understood your testimony well. So apparently you must have factual information which contradicts what Mr. Farr says, because Mr. Farr says nothing about Captain Dragan. It was other business that made him go to the Krajina. If you say, well -- don't just look at this document but also consider on what basis you testified earlier that it was for the surveillance of Captain Dragan that Mr. Simatovic left for the Krajina. Because you were positive about that, and Mr. Farr now tells you that it's his position that none of that was the reason why he went there. Any comment on the basis of your personal knowledge which led you to give the answers as you gave them earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because, in fact, Captain Dragan, and I repeat this again, was a serious threat to security in the whole region, specially in the area of Knin, and those were the reasons that I knew from my work in the Belgrade centre, that is to say continued involvement in the field was necessary. As for any other reasons, I am not aware of them. I'm talking about that time. Later, of course, after a number of years, the well-known Frenki's men were everywhere. I don't believe they reached America, but there were all sorts of rumours, but my specific knowledge is within the limits of what I stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not very precise, because you do not tell us whether it was Mr. Simatovic himself who told you, "I go there because I have to be involved in the surveillance of Captain Dragan," or whether you received any reports directly linking the presence of Mr. Simatovic to the surveillance of Captain Dragan. You have not given us any details, which I'd like to hear if you have them available. If you don't have those, then of course your source of knowledge seems to be at least a bit vague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have any opportunity to get direct insight into reports, if there were any, but considering that Mr. Dragan Filipovic had also travelled to Knin for the same reasons as I was told, it's only on the basis of immediate exchange of information and experience gained in Knin did I gain the impression that Daniel Snedden was the main target of their work, the main reason for their going to Knin. I'm not saying there were no other reasons. I'm just saying what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you say, "I gained the impression," that's still, if I could say, soft language. It's a kind of a conclusion you drew your self on the basis of the -- of the risk Mr. Snedden may have caused that you concluded that this must have been the reason for Mr. Simatovic to go there, or did you have any more concrete information that that was the reason why he went there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying this once again. Apart from statements or interpretations, if you wish, by Dragan Filipovic, at that time I did not have any more precise or more specific knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, a moment ago you said: "Later on [sic], of course, after a number of years the well-known Frenki's men were everywhere." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many news reports and media reports that published even notorious untruths and facts that do not stand up to scrutiny. I cannot recall specific articles, but it was more of a -- of an exaggeration, a blown-up image of these Frenki's men.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we please have P1062 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I meanwhile, Mr. Farr, I -- even if I already calculate the time I took for questions, that we are close to the 15 minutes you said you would need.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: This is my last document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, the title of this document is "Some Information on Daniel Snedden, Australian Citizen, Alias Kapetan Dragan." It's dated 28 August, 1991. And if we go to the bottom of page 3 in both languages, we can see that it was authored -- we can see that it was authored by Colonel Milorad Boskovic, the chief of the 3rd Department of the Security Administration of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, and it was delivered to general Kadijevic, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If we could go back to the top of the first page in both languages, please, I'll beginning reading at the beginning of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: "By the mid-June of the current year, security organs gathered the initial information on Kapetan Dragan engaged in the training of the special unit of the SAO Krajina MUP in the village of Golubic near Knin. In spite of the fact that a lot of misinformation were passed regarding his identity, the fact that he was always around and closely connected with several organs of the MUP of Serbia who were engaged on the same mission," and then there's a footnote, "indicated that we are talking about an organ or person engaged on behalf of the MUP of Serbia." If we scroll to the bottom of the page, we will see that the footnote from the previous sentence specifically identifies the "several organs of the MUP of Serbia who were engaged on the same mission as "Franko Stamatovic aka Frenki, Dragoljub Filipovic aka Fico, inspectors of the public security station of the MUP of Serbia, et cetera. Legends were created around the identity of this group as well as the identity of Kapetan Dragan." Sir, there are some mistakes with names here, and Colonel Boskovic incorrectly identified Filipovic and Simatovic with public security rather than state security --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to object. That's a comment. I mean, we don't know that. We don't know whether they've been misidentified as playing that role in addition to other roles.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash is correct. I'm putting my position, but I should have made that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, our position is that Colonel Boskovic made mistakes with the names and that he mistakenly identified Mr. Simatovic and Mr. Filipovic with public security than state security. Other than that, though, it is our position that his report is an approximate reflection of reality. Mr. Simatovic and Mr. Filipovic really were engaged in the same mission as Captain Dragan, that is, training the special unit of the SAO Krajina MUP, and Captain Dragan really was engaged on behalf of the MUP of Serbia. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any closer knowledge, but what caught my eye is the terminology used by Mr. Boskovic. He said it's about an organ or person, which means that he hasn't really identified him. He is just assuming on the basis of what he knows. It's not precise. I'm becoming aware of the rules that apply in this court concerning interpretations, but that is what I notice about this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And could we now please have the top of the next page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And I'll read the first full paragraph: "SDB of the MUP of Serbia applied measures in the case of Snedden from his arrival to the country. By monitoring his behaviour and assessing that he altered his previous orientation, they established operative contact with Snedden and sent him through the Association of Serbs from Croatia to SAO Krajina in the capacity of an instructor or as a person with no party orientation." Sir, our position is that even if the DB did monitor Captain Dragan, they also co-operated with him, and that their monitoring activities were no bar to their co-operation with Captain Dragan. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may ask you to repeat the last sentence. I didn't quite understand it. What was no bar to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The fact that the DB may have monitored Captain Dragan did not prevent the DB from also co-operating with Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say, unlike you put it, is that the DB certainly monitored Captain Dragan. Now, whether co-operation was established or was it just an operative combination allowing them to approach the target as much as possible is a matter up for debate. Professionally speaking, you have to assess it and make a decision. It is sometimes advisable to approach even your enemy to be able to evaluate his activities. Especially since I don't understand these connotations, a person with no party affiliation, what does it mean? I mean, I know what it means, but what did the author mean to say with this? And in any case, as an instructor of whatever technique related to security, he would be interesting. It's -- it's a piece of information that is interesting from the security point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, before I conclude my examination, I'd just like to tell you the Prosecution's position regarding your evidence so you can comment on it if you wish to. Our position is that you've been less than completely honest with the Chamber and that you have withheld information in your knowledge that you believe might be harmful to the accused. Do you wish to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sincerely sorry if that is the impression or the position of anyone in this courtroom. I have mentioned several times that the information and some of my documents presented here were gathered more or less in passing fashion through my operative work. So my knowledge is extremely peripheral to the issues treated by this court. I don't know what more I could say at this point, but I would like to see you refute it. Not that I would like my testimony to be refuted, but I would like you to put forward some arguments to support this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, thank you for answering my questions today.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So for you it would be further cross without having put questions to the witness. That's questions triggered by the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give us an indication as how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Twenty minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Twenty minutes. Yes. And, Mr. Bakrac, could you give us an indication already on how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think I will need more than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but could we try to -- to conclude in this section, in this -- in this session so that we could start with the next witness. I don't know whether it will be possible or not in view of the time, but let's -- let's give it a try, to see whether we can conclude the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just returning to the subject of what Simatovic was doing in Knin and what you were told he was doing. Effectively you're saying you have to look at the situation to be able to see whether he was there as an operative connection or whether he was there having established co-operation; correct? You have to look at the situation.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you put the question a bit more precisely. I didn't catch your drift.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me try it a different way. You gave evidence that you'd spoken to Filipovic, and it was Filipovic who had led you to believe that Simatovic had been sent to Knin to observe Dragan; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What did Filipovic say?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be brief. It was about the fact that he was telling us or retelling us something about his immediate operative engagement with Daniel. As far as I can remember, it was related to classic measures and activities such as surveillance, documenting, and similar things, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And your position is that whether Simatovic went further than that you can't say one way or another?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to my colleague Jordash. Page 40, line 1. The witness was more precise about the specific kind of documenting. Maybe he could be asked to repeat this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you elicit? There -- apparently there may be a part missing of the answer. Perhaps you read the last line of the answer and ask what he said in addition to what you read.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You just testified as follows according to the transcript. Please let us know if that's what you said. "As far as I can remember, it was related to classic measures and activities such as surveillance, documenting, and similar things, more or less." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something similar. However, I used different terminology. Surveillance as a measure undertaken by the State Security Department means that somebody's physically being followed, and then there is audio and photo documentation. That is another measure by the State Security Department applied within the operative engagement. There may have been something else, but I think that that's it. And as far as I know, those measures were applied to Daniel Snedden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It looks, Mr. Bakrac, the answer is now accurately on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And just so you're clear, Mr. Witness, it's Mr. Stanisic's case that that is exactly why Mr. Simatovic was sent to Knin. Now, just to be clear, your evidence is that you can provide evidence as to why he was sent, but you don't know what he eventually did when in Knin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it simply, I have no direct knowledge, because I was not in Knin, and I already stated what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did Filipovic speak to you about what he did, having been sent to Knin to observe Dragan? Are you able to say anything about what Filipovic did, having been sent for that mission?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, both Dragan Filipovic and Franko Simatovic, as far as I know, were sent there on the same task, and that was Daniel Snedden.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I'm asking you -- we've established you can't say what Mr. Simatovic did, and I'm asking you whether you know anything about what Mr. Filipovic did, having been sent on that mission. Did he stick to that mission or did he go past that mission? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than what I have already stated, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just a question about your professional roles. We looked at

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's me just quickly pick up on Vaso Mijovic. Perhaps you've answered this, but let me be sure. Are you able to confirm that he was never formally employed by the DB? I don't think you received the name. Are you able to confirm that Vaso Mijovic was never formally employed by the DB?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was told at the celebration in Kula in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the DB procedure, if he'd been formally employed, would have been that Mr. Stanisic or the chief of the service would have had to sign for that formal employment. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either Mr. Stanisic or a person authorised by him within the State Security Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Whereas if he'd been a member of the reserve force or simply associated himself with a member of the DB, there's nothing in the rules which would dictate that Mr. Stanisic would have necessarily had to be aware of that or authorise that; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All administration issues and the status issues of anybody working within the department, which includes freelancers or reserve personnel, were in the competency of the then-8th department of the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last sentence of your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only competent administration for status issues was the 8th Administration. That means that the signature should have been the signature of the head of this administration, the signature on all similar decisions, and his name I think was Milan Prodanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, 65 ter 5611, e-court page 78 and e-court B/C/S page 78.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What's coming up on the screen, I hope, is a notebook of Mr. Mladic. You saw part of it when my learned friend cross-examined you on events in Banja Luka which had involved Filipovic in 1995. What -- you were shown part of the document which suggested -- or part of the notebook which suggested a particular purpose for Serbian MUP involvement in the events, and I want to ask you about another part of the diary at e-court page 78. Dated, as you can see, 3rd of October, 1995, and there's a meeting, it seems, with Bozovic and Filipovic and Mladic, and Bozovic is quoted to have said: "I am from General Bozovic's house. We came with a task you are aware of. It was agreed that we would replace the RS police and that they would go to forward defence line." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So you followed me at least?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, there's been evidence in this courtroom that Serbian MUP police officers were sent to the Banja Luka region in September of 1995. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that's, Your Honours, D00522, Defence witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood the question correctly, whether I know anything about the engagement of the public security department of the Ministry of the Interior in Bosnia, I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, then you shorten my questions. Thank you very much. No more questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jordash. Simatovic Defence, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I want us to be focussed and brief so that we can finish before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, have you had the opportunity to see this document, decision whereby a pistol is awarded? Have you had the opportunity to see this document during the proofing session?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the document we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like the Prosecution to confirm that we have announced this document on the 21st of May as a document that may be used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any problem with that? Or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no reason to doubt it. I haven't checked Mr. Bakrac's list recently, but I have no reason to doubt his representation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, does this document fall within your personnel file that was provided to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personnel file as well as the copy that was provided to me, and that was the basis on which I didn't have to pay any more taxes for this particular weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was there any reason for you to hide the fact that you've received this weapon as an award?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe not everybody will like it, but I'm proud of it. I'm proud of the reasons because of which I received this award.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this decision has anything to do with the JATD or JSO?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely why I was surprised by the question. I truly never had any foreknowledge or any indicia that JATD had anything to do with the pistol that I was awarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1699 will receive number D1119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1119 is admitted into evidence. No need to have it under seal, Mr. Bakrac, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, could we take a look now at D900. My learned colleague Mr. Farr asked you a number of questions about the position of Franko Simatovic within the 2nd Administration of the State Security Department. Could you please take a look at this decision dated the 28th of August, 1995, whereby head of the department is changing the salary coefficient for the month of August of 1995 downwards, minus 20 per cent. And it says: Franko Simatovic, employee of the State Security Department as a special advisor at the State Security Department. Could it be possible that the head of the department does not actually know the workplace, the function of Mr. Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about Franko Simatovic, I think that there was no dilemma that he was employed by Mr. Stanisic. And even if he maybe didn't know details of a particular person, he always has the possibility to consult the 8th Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, did anybody within the State Security Department -- was there a possibility that anybody could work on two jobs at the same moment and have two decisions for that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic. Now can we take a look at 65 ter 6175. I'm not quite sure whether it was awarded the P number in the meantime. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, 6537 is the 65 ter number. I misspoke. 6537 is the 65 ter. P1365 is also the number that it was assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, this document is also a document that you signed. So we see that this is 1995, and the previous decision is also from 1995. Did this advisor in the State Security Department have an assistant for logistics?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why paragraph two, when you say that with the mentioned Dada Jovanovic a certain Mijovic entered into an intimate relationship, and he presents himself as her -- as Franko's logistics assistant? Why did you place that under quotation marks?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, that was nonsense, so it was highly likely that Mijovic was lying too, if that Mijovic existed in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps for your information, Mr. Bakrac, the provisional verification of -- of what the witness said about that Mijovic or a certain Mijovic, I read to you the relevant portion of this, again provisional, but perhaps important for you already to know. The witness, after review of the audio, but there may be some unclarity as to what he said exactly, but the verification leads to the following: "No. It's precisely what I stated in the document, that she knows about it and that she even I believe had an intimate relationship at the time with that Mijovic who even here held himself out to be Franko's assistant for logistics and also a certain Radonjic, chief of the RDB of the MUP of Serbia, and a certain Radonjic in Petrova Gora." That is as far as the CLSS was able to rehear that portion and to verify the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Micic, I have two more documents and perhaps three questions only and then I'll be done. 2420, page number 1, please. Mr. Micic, my learned friend Mr. Farr asked you about some signatures, but what we see up here is ZNRDB. Can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That that note was sent along the line of hierarchy to the deputy chief of the RDB, and when a circle is placed around it, that means that he was made aware of it. He familiarised himself with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know what happens in such cases? Who makes the decision about the possible opening of a file and the registration of this kind of file?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, that is the decision of that organisational unit itself. However, with the verification, that's the expression that is used, of the institution -- or, rather, it is the immediate superior within the hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic. Tell me - one more question, one more document, and I'll finish on that note - do you have any direct knowledge or did you hear of Franko Simatovic in September and October 1995 of him being in Bijeljina or in the area of Banja Luka and the Banja Luka Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We should have returned into open session before the break, but -- Then the Prosecution has requested a of Witness Novakovic to be further cross-examined. Are you ready to further cross-examine, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. And perhaps there's no need to repeat that, but at the time, the Chamber decided on a request for protective measures by the Republic of Serbia, and the outcome was that Mr. Novakovic would testify in open court but whenever the questions or the answers would touch upon the identity of a person who acted as a BIA source or the identity of a BIA operative or a location used by the security services, that the parties then, or the witness, would request that we would move in private session. That decision stands and is still valid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back in this courtroom. The Prosecution had received some new documentary material, and they would like to ask you some further questions about that. That's the reason why you were recalled as a witness. Thank you very much for coming again to The Hague. And since it's such a long time ago, I'll invite you to again make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Novakovic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll now be further cross-examined by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution, and you find him to your right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Novakovic. Thank you for returning to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 1 of 65 ter 6545. The Prosecution requests that this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone for the sake of interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, since your testimony last fall, the Prosecution has acquired your personnel file from BIA. Before you is a decision from your file dated 14 May 1992, which appoints you to the position of high inspector. Directing your attention to the lower left corner, did you sign this decision and acknowledge that you received it on 13 July 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At transcript page 13929 of your testimony last fall, you stated: "I was an operative in charge of counter-intelligence." And, "I was in charge of operative work which included applying all tactical operational measures." As a high inspector, did you have any supervisory responsibilities at the Uzice DB between July 1992 and November 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: From July 1992 until when? November 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That is correct, sir. That is the time period I'm asking about.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I've already said that I spent most of my time at the centre carrying out the duties that you referred to, and then towards the end of 1994 I went outside the Uzice centre because I went on mission until July 1995. So I was at the Uzice centre from time to time. Actually, I only left it from time to time, for example, during the hostage crisis, and then I went to the Krajina from July until August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that wasn't exactly my question. I was wondering if your duties and responsibilities that you performed entailed any type of supervisory or managerial work.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, as an experienced man at that time at the Uzice centre, I also did have some supervisory duties when I talked to some of our employees from other centres that were involved in counter-intelligence. So as an operative, I also had a role to supervise and co-ordinate, because if you understand me correctly, as a line operative who was specifically working on counter-intelligence, I worked on that. That only, that is. Whereas territorial employees who worked as detached employees of the centre work in the field covering all areas including counter-intelligence. If their information had to do with the field of counter-intelligence, then I would be made aware of that along the lines of counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On transcript page 13930, you testified about how your job changed once the former Yugoslavia began to fall apart. You stated: "I was still mainly preoccupied with counter intelligence as my core task. However, on occasion I was used for different purposes as well. Most of the issues we dealt with were part of the work of the 3rd Administration, which was terrorism and extremism." Is it correct that you also worked closely with the 3rd Administration operatives from the Uzice DB between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Absolutely. At the request of the leadership of the centre, I was involved in particular tasks that had to do with extremism and terrorism, but specific tasks. A few times. That is to say, this was not an ongoing task of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit D445. The Prosecution requests that this document not be broadcast to the public. The Prosecution has a hard copy of this document in court to assist the witness with his evidence. Could the court usher please provide this hard copy to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, this is a 3rd Administration official record of an interview, dated 31 January 1992. You provided comments on this document in a chart completed last fall. You stated in the chart: "I agree with everything in this document. This person knows the situation very well." You have the document before you, and I understand it's been some time since you may have seen it. If you need to review the document, please do so. But could you please let us know: Do you recall reviewing this document and making those comments?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall reading this document last autumn, and I made those comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Please do not say the name of the individual if you know, but do you know the identity of the source in this report?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can guess who the source is in view of the time period, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Weber, I should update the witness again on the -- on the protective measures. Mr. Novakovic, I don't know whether you remember, but you're testifying mainly in open session, but whenever your answers might touch upon the identity of a source or an operative of the BIA, then you should ask for private session. So that's also the reason why Mr. Weber said "don't mention the name," because we are at this moment in public session. Similar applies -- it similarly applies to any location used by the IBA [sic]. So therefore, if Mr. Weber puts any further questions to you which in answering them would reveal the identity, for example, of this source, he should ask, first of all, but otherwise you should ask for private session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we could please have the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that you are familiar with the identity of the operative who signed this report?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know if this operative is still an active member of BIA?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. He was retired before I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Returning to your comment that you provided in your comment chart, is the person who you referred to as knowing the situation very well the source of the information in this report or the operative who authored the report?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: When I mention it, I meant, first of all, the operative acting in that area, the man who was the operative officer covering the area bordering on Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, out of caution, could we please move to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, just going back to the source of the report, you mentioned that you believed you may know who this individual is. Could you please tell us the name of that individual and the basis that you believe it is this person?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: The service's source of information are the greatest asset of every service. I can guess that this is most probably Risto Perisic from Visegrad, who was at that time chief of the SUP. And with your permission, your question was -- your question said that this was a document indicating that this information was made available to the 3rd Administration, dealing with extremism. That was a time when the state was falling apart. All the subject matter covered in this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I appreciate that you like to explain. However, if you could please listen to my questions, and you've answered my questions sufficiently so far. If I need to, I will ask you further questions. Returning to the operative, Mihajlo Lukic, did you know this operative prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For how long did you know him prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: From the time he joined the department and the Uzice centre. I didn't know him before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know the year that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I joined on the 1st of February, 1977, and he came later, but I can't remember exactly when. I was with the service from the start, and he had previously been employed somewhere in the industry or business. I can't -- can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: You know, this was over 30 years ago. It could be 1978 or 1979. 1979. I don't know. Or maybe 1977. I can't say with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand the passage of time. Do I understand you correctly that you knew Mihajlo Lukic for quite some time before 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: We had been working in the service for more than ten years together by that time. I knew him very well. And I still do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with his activities between 1992 and 1995 based on your position at the Uzice DB centre?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I was. Mihajlo Lukic was a territorial officer based in Bajina Basta. He covered that area bordering on Bosnia-Herzegovina on all lines of work that the Uzice centre was working on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is Mihajlo Lukic related to either Milan Lukic or Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he is a distant relative of theirs, three or four times removed. It's a very large family, the Lukics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I know because the papers wrote about it later. In fact, I even asked him once myself. He said, Yes, I'm a distant relative. But when you say that in our language, "distant relative," that means four or five times removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At transcript page 14034 of your earlier testimony, you discussed

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: to Banja Luka as part of your team. When did you go to Banja Luka with Mihajlo Lukic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think it was in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long did you work with Mihajlo Lukic in this assignment?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: He worked with me on that assignment in 1996, 1997, in the area of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of Exhibit D744 for the witness. This exhibit contains a set of still photographs from a video admitted as P1592. If we could please have the photo enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, I'd like to direct your attention to the individual in the camouflage uniform on the right side of this image, the man standing behind the open hand in the photo. Is it correct that this individual is Mihajlo Lukic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: I couldn't say with any certainty that it's him. It looks like him, but I'm not sure. I can't be positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would it assist you to see the video of this?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour -- Your Honour, the Prosecution will prepare that for tomorrow, and we will continue at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, whether it would assist the witness, he would know once he has seen it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At transcript pages 14042 to -43 of your earlier testimony, you were asked about the situation in Bajina Basta, in Skelani in 1993 and whether the situation was of special interest to you in the service. You stated: "Absolutely. That was a direct threat on the territory which was then within the catchment area of our centre, and I believe that the leadership of the service was informed about the situation on the ground." What did you see or hear in 1993 which made you believe that the leadership of the service was informed and concerned about this situation?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, and I can't say the exact date, it was a long time ago, but towards the end of 1993, I think there was an attack on the bridge in Skelani, a border bridge between Bajina Basta and Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, between Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was a direct attack practically on the territory of Serbia. I believe even one shell landed in the centre of Bajina Basta during that attack. That confirmed the threat to the population of Bajina Basta and the centre for us in the intelligence centre, because there had been border incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How is it that you know that the leadership of the service was concerned with these events?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Not only the leadership of the service, but the leadership of the entire state was very concerned, because it was the beginning of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina when loads of people started flowing in into Serbia. Any large inflow of population from another state into Serbia is already a cause for concern. The service was tasked directly by the state with preserving the security of the country, and we had to display some concern because already at that time there had been incidents, border incidents and other incidents, and you remember we discussed them in 1992 and early 1993. That disrupted the security situation in Serbia, and the very proximity of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina raised the state of alert in our service to a higher level, because we were one the organs charged with security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You further testified when you were last here that a few operatives from the Uzice centre went to assist with the situation. Was Mihajlo Lukic one of these operatives?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Mihajlo Lukic was an operative based in Bajina Basta itself. He lived there, he worked there, and he covered the territory that he covered. But as the situation became more and more complex in Bajina Basta and the border belt, I believe additional operatives were sent to him from the Uzice on several occasions because he could not manage the entire workload on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please return to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please return to 65 ter 6545, this time page 2 of the B/C/S original and page 3 of the English translation. The Prosecution again requests that the 65 ter number not be shown to the public. Mr. Novakovic, this is a decision from your personnel file dated 16 January 1995, which is from Jovica Stanisic. Directing your attention again to the lower left-hand corner of this document, does your signature appear in this corner, and did you acknowledge receiving this decision on 26 January 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this decision, Mr. Stanisic augmented your salary by 20 per cent for the month of January 1995. The section entitled "Statement of reasons" indicates you showed above-average engagement and achieved extraordinary results. Were you assigned outside of the territory of the republic of Serbia at or near the time of this decision?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Recalled]
utterances.text: Let me tell you now, looking back and looking at this document, I can tell you exactly what it was about. The date here is 26 January 1995. From the 5th or 6th of November until 15 December 1994, I was assigned to tasks and missions in the Republic of Serbian Krajina. In our service, you got awards only on the basis of your performance and specific results, and before this there was no chance for me to earn an award, because I was not entitled to a special remuneration, only daily allowances for days spent in the Krajina, and this is the solution they -- they found to remunerate me.
